request.claim: ITU's Facts and Figures 2023 estimated that 67% of the global population used the Internet, but the corresponding figures were 93% in high-income countries and 27% in low-income countries. The global average therefore did not describe equal Internet use across these income groups.
request.context: A digital-market research brief cites https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2023/10/10/ff23-internet-use/ . Verify each attributed figure and the population groups against this original publication. Assess the historical 2023 claim rather than substituting current-year statistics.

response.explanation: The original ITU Facts and Figures 2023 Internet use page reports the same 2023 figures cited in the claim: approximately 67% of the world's population online, 93% Internet use in high-income countries, and 27% in low-income countries. The page explicitly frames these as income-group comparisons, with income groups based on the World Bank classification. Because the reported high-income and low-income figures differ by 66 percentage points, the claim's conclusion that the global average did not describe equal Internet use across those income groups is supported by the source.

evidence.text: ITU Facts and Figures 2023 states that approximately 67% of the world's population, or 5.4 billion people, was online in 2023, while 33% was offline.
The same ITU page states that in 2023 the share of people using the Internet in high-income countries rose to 93%.
The same ITU page states that in low-income countries, 27% of the population uses the Internet, and identifies a 66 percentage-point gap between high-income and low-income countries and regions.
The ITU page specifies that income groups are according to the World Bank classification, confirming that the cited high-income and low-income categories are income groups in the publication.
